# Requirements

Cody is a specialized coding agent serving both engineers and vibe coders, productizing the discipline Matrix was built with — recall-first memory, spec-driven planning, dependency-waved tasks, no-fakes verification, honest partials, complete artifacts — as STRUCTURAL engine enforcement, not prompting. Architecture (user-locked 2026-07-02): a NEW top-level cody/ module (sibling of neo/) importing the battle-tested Neo internals (llm client, cortex continuous-memory, delegate failure taxonomy, supervisor durability) but owning a coding-native loop. The orchestrator NEVER writes code: it Plans, Specs, Delegates — spawning ONE worker subagent per TASK (sequential, one alive at a time), handing it a self-contained unambiguous task sheet, independently verifying the turn-in (re-running verification + goal-vs-outcome adjudication), then accepting (checkpoint to cortex, discard worker transcript) or re-dispatching bounded with failure classification. Implementation noise never enters the orchestrator's window — that is what sustains long-horizon workloads. Modes = Prototype / Engineer / Architect: a policy tuple (planning depth, verify cadence, creativity, autonomy, explanation register); the constitution (no fakes, verify-before-done, read-full, honest partials, complete artifacts, user drives git, respect the project) binds in EVERY mode. Foundation (P1 of this same spec): migrate the per-user environment from Fly Machines to Railway — a deployed service + volume running Ubuntu 24.04 that hosts the entire daemon stack PLUS a baked dev toolchain, with /workspace on the volume; wake-on-request preserves scale-to-zero. Cody skips MCL entirely (coding is not value-moving; no core_execute, no signing). Reuses the existing arsenal: agents/cody.json over the deployed MCP bridges (fs/exec/git/browser/fetch/web-search), rules/common + rules/<language> injected per detected stack, the 186-skill library, own gateway slot 'cody'. v1 surface = a coding workspace in apps/client (chat + mode dial, file tree, diff review, terminal, dev-server preview).

## Requirement 1: Provider-neutral provisioner abstraction in the router

**User Story:** As the operator, I want the router's machine provisioning behind a provider-neutral interface, so that the per-user environment can move to Railway without rewriting the admin/proxy/wake flows and with Fly intact as a fallback.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE router SHALL define a Provisioner interface covering ensure/create, status, wake, and destroy of a per-user environment plus its persistent volume.
2. THE existing Fly Machines client (router/internal/fly) SHALL be one conforming implementation with behavior unchanged and its existing tests green.
3. A new Railway implementation (router/internal/railway) SHALL conform to the same interface using Railway's public API, covering service + volume + deployment lifecycle.
4. THE active provider SHALL be selected by configuration (fly | railway) per deployment; admin.StartProvision, proxy.EnsureStarted, and the chronos wake path SHALL consume only the interface.
5. PROVISION status (provision_jobs, GET /provision/status) SHALL report Railway deployment readiness so the onboarding readiness gate keeps working unchanged.

## Requirement 2: Ubuntu 24.04 per-user dev-environment image

**User Story:** As a user, I want my private environment to be a full development machine, so that Cody codes where my files live with real toolchains, and my code persists on my volume.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE environment image SHALL be Ubuntu 24.04 hosting the entire existing daemon stack (MCL daemon, Neo, MCP tool bridges) plus codyd.
2. THE image SHALL bake a dev toolchain including at minimum git, build-essential, Node + pnpm, Go, Python + uv, and Rust.
3. THE persistent volume SHALL mount /data (daemon state) and /workspace (user code); /workspace SHALL remain the root served by the fs/git/exec MCP servers so the existing tool surface transfers unchanged.
4. DEV servers started via the exec bridge's supervised services SHALL be reachable for preview through the environment's networking.

## Requirement 3: Wake-on-request (scale-to-zero preserved)

**User Story:** As the operator, I want slept environments to wake on inbound traffic, so that per-user economics stay scale-to-zero on Railway without an explicit start API.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a request arrives for a slept environment, THE router proxy SHALL forward it as the wake signal and absorb cold-start latency via the existing daemon-readiness probing, within the configured wake budget.
2. THE chronos /internal/wake path SHALL wake the environment and deliver the timer-triggered turn on Railway semantics.
3. WHILE the environment is waking, THE router SHALL respond with the same retry semantics the client already handles (the provisioning/loading path), not a hard failure.
4. THE environment SHALL be outbound-quiet when idle so Railway's outbound-inactivity sleep detection engages: the periodic snapshot push ticker SHALL be disabled on Railway (boot pull retained as the volume-seed/migration vehicle; the persistent volume is the durable state), and no daemon component SHALL emit periodic outbound traffic while idle.

## Requirement 4: Cody orchestrator — Plans, Specs, Delegates; never writes code

**User Story:** As a user, I want Cody's main loop to stay a lean planner/verifier, so that it sustains long-horizon projects without drowning its context in implementation noise.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE orchestrator SHALL NOT edit files or run implementation commands; its only executions SHALL be verification re-runs and read-only inspection.
2. THE orchestrator cycle SHALL be: understand (workspace model + cortex recall) -> plan (waved task list, depth per mode) -> spec the next eligible task into a task sheet -> delegate to ONE worker -> independently verify the turn-in -> accept or re-dispatch -> loop.
3. EXACTLY ONE worker SHALL be alive at a time; delegation SHALL be per task, never per wave.
4. ON acceptance, THE worker transcript SHALL be discarded; only the turn-in report and the cortex checkpoint SHALL persist in the orchestrator's context.
5. THE orchestrator window after N accepted tasks SHALL contain the plan, task sheets, and turn-in reports — no worker implementation transcripts.

## Requirement 5: The task sheet — self-contained delegation contract

**User Story:** As a worker, I want a detailed unambiguous implementation sheet for exactly one task, so that I can execute with zero conversation history.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EACH task sheet SHALL carry: the goal (what done means), testable acceptance criteria, grounding (exact files/seams/line refs and the read-before-write set), constraints (constitution + mode policy + applicable rules/<language> refs), the verification commands that must be green, and the deliverable shape including what NOT to touch.
2. THE sheet SHALL be self-contained: a fresh-context worker SHALL be able to execute it without access to the orchestrator's conversation history.
3. SHEETS SHALL be durable records (persisted with the plan) so a crashed worker is replaceable by a fresh one from the same sheet.

## Requirement 6: The worker — fresh context, full tools, structured turn-in

**User Story:** As the orchestrator, I want workers that implement exactly one sheet and report evidence, so that acceptance is decidable from the report plus my own verification.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EACH worker SHALL start with a fresh context containing only the task sheet and a minimal grounding bundle.
2. WORKERS SHALL have the full coding tool surface (fs, exec incl. supervised services, git, browser, fetch, web-search) plus the edit engine and verification runner.
3. EACH worker SHALL return a structured turn-in report: status (done|partial|blocked), changes (path/kind/why), verification evidence (real command output), and honest gaps/assumptions.
4. IF a worker crashes or its run is lost, THE orchestrator SHALL dispatch a fresh worker from the same sheet (task durability at the task level).

## Requirement 7: Acceptance gate — independent verification + bounded re-dispatch

**User Story:** As the user, I want Cody to never take a worker's word for it, so that accepted work is genuinely done.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ON turn-in, THE orchestrator SHALL independently re-run the sheet's verification commands; acceptance SHALL be impossible without a green verification record.
2. THE orchestrator SHALL adjudicate the turn-in goal-vs-outcome (Cassandra-style: does the outcome satisfy the sheet's goal and acceptance criteria), not by string-matching the report.
3. ON rejection, THE orchestrator SHALL re-dispatch with concrete feedback, bounded by a configured attempt ceiling (default 3).
4. WORKER failures SHALL be classified via the delegate failure taxonomy; deterministic failures SHALL stop-and-ask the user instead of burning re-dispatch attempts.
5. ON acceptance, THE orchestrator SHALL write a durable progress checkpoint to cortex.

## Requirement 8: The constitution — engine-enforced invariants, every mode

**User Story:** As the user, I want unchanging quality rules that no mode can relax, so that Cody's output holds a standard it never breaks.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. NO FAKES: workers SHALL NOT introduce stub/mock/fake doubles or placeholder implementations to make verification pass; violations SHALL cause rejection at the acceptance gate.
2. VERIFY BEFORE DONE: no task SHALL be marked done without green verification + adjudication (structurally gated, not prompted).
3. READ FULL: WHEN tool output is truncated with the remainder retrievable, THE engine SHALL retrieve it in full before reasoning (overflow-file discipline), in both roles.
4. NO FALSE SUCCESS: partials SHALL surface as partials in turn-in reports and user-facing completion reports.
5. COMPLETE ARTIFACTS: deliverables SHALL be runnable with dependencies and run instructions, never fragments.
6. USER DRIVES GIT: Cody SHALL stage, diff, and propose, but commit/push only on explicit user instruction.
7. RESPECT THE PROJECT: workers SHALL follow existing repo style and SHALL NOT make drive-by comments/docs/refactors outside the sheet's scope; tests SHALL never be weakened or deleted to pass.

## Requirement 9: Modes — Prototype / Engineer / Architect as policy tuples

**User Story:** As a user, I want to dial ceremony to my intent — spike fast or build for the long haul — without ever trading away the constitution.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A MODE SHALL be a policy tuple over: planning depth, verification cadence, creativity temperature, autonomy level, and explanation register — one engine, no mode-specific loops.
2. PROTOTYPE SHALL plan tersely inline, verify at milestones and at done, favor creative opinionated defaults, and speak in outcome language.
3. ENGINEER (default) SHALL plan a waved task list and verify after every task.
4. ARCHITECT SHALL author durable spec files (EARS requirements, design, waved tasks) persisted in the workspace, verify per task with property tests, and be resumable across sessions.
5. THE constitution (req.8) SHALL bind identically in every mode.
6. MODEL policy SHALL be per role and mode-aware (orchestrator may pin a stronger model; Prototype workers may run faster models), all through the cody gateway slot.

## Requirement 10: Coding-native primitives — workspace model, edit engine, verification runner, checkpoints

**User Story:** As the engine, I want precise repo-aware primitives, so that edits are safe, verification is the project's own truth, and progress survives anything.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE workspace model SHALL maintain a persistent repo index over /workspace (tree, languages, frameworks, build targets, entry points) across sessions on the volume.
2. THE edit engine SHALL apply anchored edits with staleness detection: an edit SHALL fail if the target file changed since it was read, never blind-overwrite.
3. THE verification runner SHALL detect the project's own commands (package.json scripts, Makefile, go.mod, cargo, pytest, ...) and run build/test/lint/typecheck as first-class loop steps.
4. CHECKPOINT/ROLLBACK SHALL snapshot the workspace before risky multi-file changes and restore on request; per-task progress checkpoints SHALL persist to cortex and survive process restarts.

## Requirement 11: Standards + skills injection

**User Story:** As the user, I want Cody to hold our stack-specific standards and deep playbooks, so that its code quality is engineer-level by construction.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. CODY SHALL inject rules/common/* plus the applicable rules/<language>/* into its working policy per the detected stack, and task sheets SHALL reference the applicable rule files as constraints.
2. CODY SHALL surface the skills/ library through the existing skill mechanism as on-demand deep-domain playbooks.

## Requirement 12: Memory — cortex continuous-memory as Cody's long-horizon substrate

**User Story:** As a user, I want Cody to remember my project across sessions and machines restarts, so that long-horizon work resumes exactly where it left off.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. CODY SHALL persist per-project memory (decisions, checkpoints, story-so-far) via the cortex continuous-memory surfaces (AppendMessage / Activate / recursive recall).
2. WHEN codyd restarts or a session refreshes mid-plan, THE orchestrator SHALL resume from cortex checkpoints at the correct next task with its lean context reconstructed (plan + reports, no transcripts).

## Requirement 13: codyd server, manifest, and gateway slot

**User Story:** As the platform, I want Cody deployed like Neo — a first-class agent with its own manifest and metered slot — so that it inherits the proven serving shape.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. codyd SHALL run in the per-user environment beside Neo following the proven shape: engine + session supervisor + SSE broker + durable trace, mounted behind the router under the user's JWT.
2. agents/cody.json SHALL define Cody's tool manifest reusing the deployed MCP bridges (fs, exec, git, browser, fetch, web-search) with NO value-moving surface.
3. CODY SHALL register its own gateway LLM slot 'cody' (types slot + routing validSlot + rates whitelist entry), never borrowing another agent's slot; the rate card values remain operator-owned.
4. CODY SHALL NOT hold a signing key, SHALL NOT route through the MCL walk, and SHALL NOT modify Neo, the Liaison boundary, or the wallet seam.

## Requirement 14: Client coding workspace

**User Story:** As a user (engineer or vibe coder), I want a coding workspace in the Matrix client, so that I can direct Cody, review its work, and see my running app.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. apps/client SHALL gain a Cody coding workspace: chat with a mode selector, workspace file tree, diff review pane, live terminal attached to the environment, and dev-server preview.
2. THE surface SHALL follow the durable-trace + live-SSE reducer pattern so the workspace rebuilds on reopen.
3. THE surface SHALL show the RESULT, not the protocol (no orchestrator/worker/sheet jargon in consumer-facing copy), with the explanation register following the active mode.
4. UI house rules SHALL hold: separation by background-color contrast only (never border strokes for depth); no emojis, purple gradients, or glow effects.

## Requirement 15: Real verification — no fakes

**User Story:** As the owner, I want every pillar proven against real code paths, so that Cody ships genuinely working.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. PROVISIONER conformance SHALL be tested against recorded Railway API fixtures via httptest (mirroring fly_test.go), with the Fly implementation's existing tests still green.
2. WAKE-ON-REQUEST SHALL be proven by a proxy integration test where the first forwarded request to a slept-service simulation succeeds within the wake budget.
3. THE sheet/turn-in round-trip SHALL be proven end-to-end: a real orchestrator authors a sheet for a seeded real repo; a real worker executes it in a real workspace; the report carries real verification output.
4. THE acceptance gate SHALL be proven structural: a turn-in claiming success with red verification is rejected; a green turn-in is accepted and checkpointed to real cortex.
5. RE-DISPATCH policy SHALL be proven: deterministic failures stop-and-ask after classification; transient failures re-dispatch bounded by the ceiling.
6. CONTEXT economy SHALL be proven on the real message window: after N accepted tasks the orchestrator context holds plan + sheets + reports only.
7. DURABILITY SHALL be proven: killing codyd mid-plan and restarting resumes from cortex checkpoints at the correct next task.
8. MODES SHALL be proven: the same seeded task under Prototype vs Architect exhibits the policy differences while both hold the constitution.
9. NO test in this feature SHALL substitute a stub/mock/fake for a real code path or type to manufacture a pass.

## Requirement 16: Control-plane co-location — one Railway project/environment

**User Story:** As the operator, I want the control plane and shared tool services in the same Railway project/environment as the per-user services, so that the router reaches user environments over the private network and the prod box + Fly footprint retire completely.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE router, gateway, chronos, Postgres, and MinIO SHALL run as services in the SAME Railway project/environment as the per-user services (Railway private networking is scoped to one project+environment).
2. ONLY the router SHALL carry a public domain; gateway, chronos, Postgres, and MinIO SHALL be private-only (reachable solely via <service>.railway.internal), and the router's internal listener (/admin, /internal/wake) SHALL never be publicly exposed.
3. THE shared tool services (browser, tachyon, uwac, deus) SHALL move into the same environment, joining the already-deployed searxng/gotenberg/stalwart; daemon-visible URLs SHALL flip from Fly .internal to .railway.internal via the existing MachineEnv env overrides.
4. AUTH SHALL be the boundary on the shared private network: constant-time bearers on admin/wake/gateway, strong Postgres auth, and per-user scoped MinIO keys — since user daemons share the private network with the control plane.
